title: Auth migration: SIEM onboarding & evidence signal harmonization
body:
Executive summary:

This doc captures a pragmatic migration strategy for moving from the existing coarse permission model to RBAC v2 while simultaneously harmonizing the audit/evidence signal taxonomy and onboarding those signals into the corporate SIEM. Goal: enable a phased migration that preserves runtime compatibility for services, produces consistent evidence artifacts for compliance audits, and reduces manual investigation overhead for incident response.

Context and motivation:
- Current state: multiple services emit ad-hoc audit records (access_grant, api_call, impersonation, token_issue) with different field names and sampling policies. Evidence extraction is partially manual (security team runs scripts to gather logs for audits).
- Target state: RBAC v2 authority model (roles, attributes, grants) with a standard audit schema (fields and semantics documented below), automated evidence bundling for compliance artifacts, and SIEM-friendly exports (normalized events, enrichment, and retention flags).
- Constraints: minimal performance impact on hot paths, compatibility with Dedicated and Private deployments where some logs cannot leave customer network, and support for post-facto attestation requirements (time-windowed evidence).

High-level migration strategy (phases):

Phase 0 — Discovery & inventory (2–3 weeks):
- Compile a service matrix listing who currently enforces permissions and what signals they emit (authz checkpoints, token endpoints, policy caches).
- Map existing permission primitives to RBAC v2 concepts (roles, permissions, attributes).
- Deliverable: inventory spreadsheet + per-service gap list (will feed Phase 1).

Phase 1 — Normalized audit schema rollout (4 weeks):
- Define a minimal audit record spec (see "Audit record schema" below).
- Implement lightweight SDK shims for emitting normalized records (language: Go, Python, Node). Use feature flagging so we can toggle on per-service.
- Create CI check that validates emitted records against schema.
- Deliverable: schema repo + SDK packages + service opt-in plan.

Phase 2 — RBAC v2 pilot & evidence automation (6–8 weeks):
- Implement RBAC v2 control plane (policy storage, evaluation API) for a small set of pilot services (console, rollout API, model catalog).
- Ensure each control decision emits a normalized audit record and a corresponding evidence artifact (hash + pointer).
- Build evidence bundling lambda that, given a request id, compiles the relevant artifacts into a signed ZIP for audits.
- Deliverable: pilot runbook, sample evidence bundles for compliance.

Phase 3 — SIEM mapping and onboarding (3–4 weeks, concurrent with Phase 2):
- Create SIEM ingestion mapping for normalized records. Provide enrichment pipeline (user directory joins, role name canonicalization, region tags).
- Implement retention and masking flags: PII-sensitive fields must be masked prior to cross-tenant aggregation for Hosted API signals.
- Deliverable: SIEM ingestion docs + playbook for on-call triage using new signals.

Phase 4 — Gradual rollout & compatibility shim removal (ongoing 6–12 weeks):
- Incrementally migrate services off legacy permission checks to RBAC v2 using canary traffic + fallback policies.
- Remove legacy audit emitters once a service passes compatibility checks and evidence automation produces expected bundles for 30 days.
- Deliverable: end-of-migration checklist, postmortem templates.

Audit record schema (minimal, must be emitted for every authz decision):
- event_id: uuid4 string
- timestamp_utc: iso8601
- service: short service name (e.g., console-api)
- environment: hosted | dedicated | private
- request_id: tracing id linking upstream request
- actor: {subject_type}:{subject_id} (e.g., user:alice@example.com, token:kr_123)
- action: canonical verb (e.g., read, write, invoke, list, grant)
- resource: canonical resource path (e.g., model/rdwx/bert-7b/versions/3)

(continued)
- decision: allow | deny | fallback-allow | fallback-deny
- policy_version: semver or commit sha where policy evaluated came from
- role_bindings: list of role ids evaluated (comma-separated string in the event)
- attributes: flattened key=value pairs for attributes used in decision (e.g., region=us-west, org_id=acme)

(continued)
- evidence_ref: pointer(s) to additional artifacts (signed K/V store key, s3 path, or on-prem bundle id). For Private deployments this may be a local bundle id and a hash.
- sampling_hint: always | high | medium | low (controls whether this event should be sent to central SIEM or sampled)

Schema notes and rationale:
- Keep fields flat to simplify SIEM mapping and KQL queries. Complex nested objects complicate retention/masking rules.
- Always emit an evidence_ref when the decision is non-trivial (deny, fallback, or grant for privileged roles). Evidence can be a stack trace, policy snapshot, or a policy-eval transcript.
- The sampling_hint allows services to limit traffic to central SIEM (Hosted) while preserving a local, full-fidelity store for Dedicated/Private.

SIEM mapping and enrichment plan:
- Normalization layer (log-shipper sidecar): map event fields to SIEM schema (timestamp, host, event.action, user.name, service.name, object.id, event.outcome). Add geo-region and tenant tagging.
- Enrichment: call directory service to resolve actor -> org_id, canonical display name, role history. Append risk_score if available from runtime anomaly detection.
- Masking: PII fields (email, full ids) get redacted for cross-tenant indices; redaction can be reversible within a dedicated tenant-only index for audits.
- Alerts: define SIEM rules for high-severity signals: repeated fallback-deny on critical resources, mass-role changes in short window, evidence missing for deny events.

Evidence automation & bundling runbook (draft):
- Trigger points: periodic (daily summary), on-demand (audit request), and on-event (deny of high-privilege change).
- Bundle contents: primary audit record, policy snapshot (policy_version), evaluated attributes, relevant request traces, user session metadata, and any files e.g., policy-engine logs.
- Signing: bundles are hashed and signed by the evidence-service key. Store signature and bundle hash in the audit record's evidence_ref.
- Storage: Hosted -> central S3 with tenant-aware access controls. Dedicated -> tenant S3 or object store. Private -> local store with manifest exported to central (hash-only) for attestation.

Performance considerations & mitigations:
- Emission overhead: normalized events should be buffered and emitted asynchronously; the control path must avoid blocking on network I/O. Use local write-ahead logs when necessary.
- Size: limit embedded artifacts in events; prefer object refs and streaming uploads for large artifacts.
- Backpressure: if SIEM is slower, services should apply sampling_hint and retain full-fidelity local logs for replay.

Operational playbooks (quick reference):
- On denied critical action (console:role-grant):
  1) Triage using request_id to retrieve evidence bundle.
  2) Confirm policy_version and role_bindings.
  3) If mismatch suspected, mark policy_version as suspect and open an incident.
- On missing evidence_ref for deny events:
  1) Attempt an immediate re-index (bundle rebuild).
  2) If rebuild fails, escalate to infra with incident tag: evidence-missing.

Open questions and unresolved decisions:
- Canonical role id format: short string vs. fully qualified path? (pro: FQ is unique across orgs, con: verbosity)
- How to represent long-running grants (temporal roles) in a compact, queryable way?
- Exact sampling defaults for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (regulatory constraints may force different defaults).

Next steps (1–2 weeks):
- Approve minimal audit schema (this doc) with SRE and infra owners.
- Kick off Phase 0 inventory; create per-service opt-in trackers in the repo.
- Build the first shim for console-api in Go and validate event emission in staging.

Appendix A — Example event (single-line JSON for SIEM):
{"event_id":"d8c2a1f6-4d3b-4a6a-8b2b-9f3c6e2a7b1f","timestamp_utc":"2025-01-10T14:22:05Z","service":"console-api","environment":"hosted","request_id":"req_7a2f9c","actor":"user:maya.chen@example.com","action":"grant","resource":"role/admin","decision":"deny","policy_version":"v2.3.1","role_bindings":"role/viewer","attributes":"region=us-east,org_id=acme","evidence_ref":"s3://evidence-hosted/2025/01/10/bundles/req_7a2f9c.zip#sha256:abcd...","sampling_hint":"always"}

Appendix B — Migration acceptance checklist (per service):
- Emits normalized audit records for 100% of control decisions in staging for 7 days.
- Evidence bundles can be generated within 10s for on-demand requests.
- SIEM mapping validated: fields searchable and correctly enriched.
- Privacy masking verified for cross-tenant indices.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally prescriptive on schema to reduce ambiguity during SIEM onboarding. Feedback requested on sampling defaults and the evidence_ref canonicalization format.

Maya Chen
Lead, Security & Compliance
